info.title: OpenAsy Runtime API
info.summary: What processes do on your hosts and pods, from Falco: detections with their process tree, the programs that ran, and changes to watched files.
info.description:
Every screen of Runtime uses this API, and so can your scripts (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only; anything removed is deprecated first. Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457).

runtime-agent enrols with a one-time or fleet enrolment token at `/api/v1/agent/enroll` and then calls `/api/v1/agent/*` with its own secret, which speaks for its host only. Everything else takes the session of a signed-in person or an API token, and each operation names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`: viewer, editor, admin; ADR 0003).

Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

200.description: Metrics in the Prometheus text format.

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` when Runtime runs on plain http://localhost). Requests that change something must come from Runtime's origin.

apiToken.description: An API token created under Settings → API tokens (`oa_runtime_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003).

adminToken.description: Only when Runtime is started by its tests or a local script: one shared token with the admin role. A production install does not have it.

agentSecret.description: The secret runtime-agent got when it enrolled (`oia_...`). It speaks for its own host only.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

pid.description: Unknown for an ancestor Falco did not name.

cmd.description: The command line, or only the program's name for older ancestors.

rule.description: The Falco rule, or Runtime's own New process in container.

process.description: The command line of the process the rule matched first.

output.description: Falco's output line of the latest event.

attack.description: MITRE ATT&CK techniques among the rule's tags.

tree.description: The processes of its events, joined by pid.

id.description: Opaque; newer events have larger ids.

source.description: Falco's event source, such as syscall, or runtime for Runtime's own rule.

file.description: The file the event is about, for opens, renames and unlinks.

result.description: alerted raised or joined a detection; kept matched a rule whose policy is off.

image.description: The container image; null for a program on the host itself.

baseline.description: known: learned or accepted. new: a program never seen on this host or image. drift: a known program with a new parent or user.

sha256.description: Null for a file larger than the agent hashes.

at.description: When the agent's read found it.

by.description: The process of the newest Falco event about this file since the read before, and its user.

severity.description: The severity its detections get: the override, or Falco's priority.

status.description: silent: no word for two minutes. sensor-down: the agent cannot reach Falco. outdated: the agent's version is not Runtime's.

dropped.description: Events the agent could not hold while Runtime was out of reach.

learningUntil.description: Until then every program the host runs is learned as known.

token.description: Shown this once. Start runtime-agent with it as RUNTIME_ENROLL_TOKEN.

new.description: Programs new or drifted, not yet accepted.

Report.description: The agent's report of itself, with every call.
